purpose: Conformance fixture for deterministic, observation-mediated synthetic actor policies. It is not a human-behaviour dataset.

rules.when: actor_state == crossing AND ego_ttc_status == observed AND ego_ttc_s <= 2.5
actor_state == waiting AND ego_ttc_status == observed AND ego_ttc_s >= 3.5
actor_state == waiting AND ego_ttc_status == observed AND ego_ttc_s <= 1.5
actor_state == waiting AND ego_ttc_status == observed AND ego_ttc_s > 1.5

synthetic_scenario.description: A synthetic pedestrian-like actor crosses a single ego lane. The case exists to test policy causality and replay, not to approximate a human population.

conformance_cases.mutation: Change only an ego command scheduled at tick 12.
conformance_cases.comparison_window: actor policy inputs, outputs, states and receipts for ticks 0 through 11

conformance_cases.mutation: Change a simulator-only ego controller mode while preserving the actor's canonical allowed observation bytes.
conformance_cases.comparison_window: actor policy output for the same actor state and tick

conformance_cases.mutation: Make a changed ego-speed cue visible at tick 4 but deliver it at tick 6.
conformance_cases.comparison_window: actor outputs at ticks 4 and 5 versus tick 6 onward
conformance_cases.expected: no response attributable to the changed cue before tick 6

conformance_cases.mutation: Mark visible_ego_speed as occluded without changing hidden world speed.
conformance_cases.expected: speed value is unavailable; policy follows its declared non-observed fallback

conformance_cases.mutation: Replace a fresh TTC cue with stale and then missing statuses in separate runs.
conformance_cases.comparison_window: transition receipts and expected outcome counts
conformance_cases.expected: statuses remain distinct and no missing value is encoded as numeric zero

conformance_cases.mutation: Compare continue, yield and accelerate ego branches with their delivered visible-motion cues.
conformance_cases.comparison_window: actor trace after the first branch-specific cue delivery
conformance_cases.expected: policy response may diverge only after the relevant cue is delivered; pre-delivery traces match
conformance_cases.failure_means: clairvoyant response or absence of declared causal sensitivity

conformance_cases.mutation: Run both policy profiles with a crossing-state actor and observed TTC of 2.0 seconds.
conformance_cases.comparison_window: next accepted actor action after reaction delay
conformance_cases.failure_means: policy identity is decorative or policy implementations collapse

conformance_cases.mutation: Reconstruct initial world, stable actor map, policy digests and materialized exogenous trace in a fresh process.
conformance_cases.comparison_window: every actor receipt and world snapshot by tick
conformance_cases.expected: bitwise equality under the same named runtime profile

conformance_cases.mutation: Run the fixed trajectory baseline under multiple ego-action histories.
conformance_cases.expected: the baseline remains marked open_loop_script and cannot satisfy interactive_policy acceptance

conformance_cases.mutation: Inject duplicate actor IDs, duplicate per-actor sequence, backward tick, NaN, infinity or out-of-profile speed.
conformance_cases.expected: rejected or explicitly modified-with-receipt; never silently accepted

claim_ceiling: observation-mediated response under declared information boundaries
same-runtime replay under named execution profile
